messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: model-warmup-errors on us-west-2-prod-serving (sev=2) - paging oncall @raja

maya: seeing repeated model load failures on a subset of warmup pods. quick summary: several nodes OOM during deserialization, then subsequent compile timeouts. Started ~1712004300 UTC.

lee: logs show repeated `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED` when trying to allocate 1.9G for kv cache during warmup. also seeing `failed to mmap` lines right before the OOM.

raja: oncall acked, jumping in. which model and which build?

maya: model: open-llama-70b-v2-quant (redwood-optimized build 2026-02-10), warmup job tries to load full 8k context. artifact sha: `3f2a9b`. I see some deserialization stack: `serde_json::from_slice` throwing `IOError: short read` in the warmup path.

lee: that short read is interesting — could be truncated artifact or transient io stall while streaming weights. but the cublas alloc fail indicates memory fragmentation or not enough free VRAM. nodes with older kernels show more failures.

maya: here's the paste of the warmup pod tail (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-05T18:05:12Z] warmup: loading artifact 3f2a9b
[2026-03-05T18:05:13Z] warmup: deserializing layer 0 (offset 0x1f4)
[2026-03-05T18:05:13Z] warmup: serde error: short read
[2026-03-05T18:05:13Z] warmup: retrying fetch
[2026-03-05T18:05:14Z] warmup: successfully fetched chunk 0
[2026-03-05T18:05:15Z] runtime: attempting GPU alloc 1953125000 bytes
[2026-03-05T18:05:15Z] runtime: cuda error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED (cuBLAS)
[2026-03-05T18:05:15Z] runtime: falling back to host staging
[2026-03-05T18:05:16Z] warmup: compile kernel timed out (120s)
[2026-03-05T18:05:16Z] kubelet: oomkilled process 1823 (model-warmup)
```

raja: thanks. immediate mitigations recommended: 1) disable warmup on the failing pool (so we avoid repeated OOM churn), 2) route new requests to the quantized fallback model (smaller KV usage), 3) cordon problematic nodes and recycle them. Lee - can you run `kubectl` to disable warmup?

lee: running now. command: `kubectl -n serving patch configmap warmup-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/warmupEnabled","value":false}]'` 

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered rollout: warmup toggle -> patch applied to serving configmap in us-west-2-prod.

maya: patched. warmup jobs should stop spawning within 30s. I'll watch the job controller logs.

sophia: any customer impact? I see increased 503s for a handful of high-QPS customers on us-west-2. Need to surface to CS.

raja: looking at metrics - 95th latency spiked from 220ms to 1.2s for text-generation route for the affected pool. error budget hit for a small percentage (0.8% increase in error rate). I will open a CSE ticket and update the status page if this persists.

lee: cordoning nodes with repeated OOMs: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17` and `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets gpu-node-17 --delete-local-data`. scheduling restart.

maya: also noticed the artifact fetch retried a few times with partial chunks. provider reported transient S3 5xx in that AZ around the same time. could be combination: partial artifact leading to deserialization retries then larger memory pressure once reassembled.

raja: good catch. for immediate risk reduction, enable fallback routing: `redwood route set --from model=open-llama-70b-v2-quant --to model=open-llama-70b-v2-8bit --percent=100 --region=us-west-2` (this routes traffic away from the failing variant). ops-bot please run.

ops-bot: routing command executed. traffic now directed to open-llama-70b-v2-8bit in us-west-2.

maya: after routing change, error rates back down to baseline for most customers. a few long-running streams saw reconnects but recovered.

sophia: I posted a heads-up to #customers-public about transient errors in us-west-2; CS already reached out to the three affected customers.

lee: repro attempt: spun up a single warmup pod with large context and used `strace` — saw `mmap` EAGAIN in kernel logs before OOM. Also kernel version on node `5.15.0-102` vs `5.15.0-108` differ; older kernel seems to fragment GPU memory more aggressively for our driver. Ops: recommend not scheduling warmup on older-kernel hosts until we patch driver.

ops-bot: action items noted: disable warmup on old-kernel nodes; schedule firmware/driver upgrade in maintenance window.

raja: I'm going to hand off to night oncall @lee in 20m. Lee, please confirm you have the mitigations and follow-up list.

lee: taking handoff. confirm: warmup disabled cluster-wide for affected pool, traffic routed to 8bit fallback in us-west-2, cordoned and rebooted two nodes (gpu-node-17/18), CS notified, postmortem owner needed. I'll monitor through 0300 UTC.

maya: owners for postmortem: maya (runtime), lee (sre), ops (infra). root cause hypotheses: (1) transient S3 5xx caused partial artifact reads -> deserialization retries; (2) kernel+driver combination increases fragmentation -> CUBLAS alloc failures; (3) compile timeouts cascade when host staging used. Next steps: artifact integrity check for sha `3f2a9b`, add checksums on fetch to fail-fast, increase compile timeout backoff and add staged fallback, and schedule kernel/driver upgrades.

raja: adding incident severity: sev2. I will create the ticket and flag for priority postmortem.

sophia: please add a short customer-facing blurb for the status page: "We experienced transient model load failures affecting inference in us-west-2 between 18:05–18:32 UTC causing higher error rates for a small subset of customers. Traffic was routed to a fallback model and affected nodes were isolated. We are investigating root cause and will follow up."

maya: logging the timeline and attaching the warmup logs + kernel traces to the incident ticket.

lee: monitoring shows stable after mitigation; re-enabling warmup will require a canary with patched driver and artifact checksum validation.

ops-bot: handoff checklist created and assigned to lee; scheduled follow-up meeting in 4 hours.

raja: handing off to lee now. If anything regresses, ping me directly.

lee: accepted handoff — will keep watch and start the postmortem draft. closing page for now unless new alerts. :white_check_mark:
